purpose: Economic materiality: which members' AI/data-centre economics are already large enough to matter, as distinct from admission (thematic evidence) and sizing (liquidity). A member stays in the basket either way; this is a tier within it.

text: Evidence test: at least one filed order, committed capex or operating disclosure on the company's own paper. Aspiration alone does not count.

Materiality test, any one of: Rs 100 cr or more of AI/data-centre revenue or executable orders; 5% or more of company revenue from AI/data centres; 5% or more of FY26 EBITDA from AI/data centres by FY29 in AGI's base case; a contracted position (MW or GW) with a named customer that is 5% or more of the company's own capacity.

Safeguards, both required: evidence confidence medium or high; a path from order or capacity to revenue within about 36 months (revenue already booked, a timeline the company states, order cover of 12 quarters or less, or AGI's FY29 horizon for an estimate-only pass).
Strict on amounts: an order with no disclosed value, share or named-customer MW does not count, however strong the evidence that it exists.
A pass that rests only on AGI's estimate counts, and is labelled as an estimate.
